result:
My final answer scores **0.5648 on the search split**, up from the baseline's 0.365. I used **14 of the 24 scorer calls** and about 13 of my 15-minute budget. I stopped there because the last few rounds were adding less than 0.001 per idea. The held-out score hasn't been taken yet: the only split I've seen is search, so the held-out check below is on my own simulated traces.

| | search (scorer) | held-out (my local traces) |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline (LRU) | 0.365 | 0.418 |
| First champion (W-TinyLFU) | 0.503 | — |
| **Final (`final.py`)** | **0.5648** | **0.519** |

**How it works.** `final.py` runs five eviction policies side by side as simulations: ARC and four W-TinyLFU caches whose frequency counts fade at different speeds (every 4, 16 and 256 × capacity requests). Each simulation keeps a running hit count that weights recent requests more. The real cache copies whichever one is currently ahead. When it switches, it only adds the key just requested and drops keys the new leader doesn't hold, so it stays within the rules. It only switches when the challenger is clearly ahead, which stops it flipping back and forth.

**Why it beats LRU.** No single policy wins on every kind of trace. TinyLFU holds on to part of a loop that's too big for the cache, and to hot keys during one-off scans; on loop traces LRU hits about 0.2–0.3 and TinyLFU about 0.65. ARC wins when recent use is what matters (0.85 against TinyLFU's 0.60–0.75). Following the current leader gets close to the best policy on every trace. The whole run takes about 3.8s, against the 8s limit.

**Approaches tried first:**

| Approach | Search score |
|---|---|
| ARC | 0.407 |
| W-TinyLFU | 0.503 |
| S3-FIFO | 0.464 |
| W-TinyLFU, adaptive window size | not scored (worse locally) |
| W-TinyLFU, adaptive fade speed | not scored (worse locally) |

**Candidate log:**

| + recently rejected keys get in when they come back | 0.560 | 0.531 | dropped: loops got worse |
| Follow the leader: TinyLFU vs ARC | 0.597 | 0.554 | kept |

| + extra TinyLFU with a bigger window, or faster fading | 0.603 | — | dropped |
| Fading speeds 4/16/64 | 0.6045 | 0.564 | kept |
| Fading speeds 4/16/256 | 0.6045 | **0.5648** | **final** |
| Smaller protected section (0.5) | 0.601 | — | dropped |
| Add speed 2 | — | 0.5650 | dropped: within noise, 25% slower |
| Longer scoring horizon, margin 20 | — | 0.562 | dropped |

My local traces didn't rank candidates quite like the scorer. They underweight loops, which is why TinyLFU came third locally but first on the scorer. So I used the scorer for choices the local traces couldn't separate. The hot-with-scans and mixed traces stay around 0.25–0.28 for every policy I tried; I didn't measure how far below the best possible that is.
